person.name: Rowena Ocampo
person.traits: Twenty years on floors like this one. Does not negotiate, does not raise her voice, and does not lie where a denial will do.

start.prompt: The fourth floor is quieter than the third. Forty desks, forty headsets, and at the back a desk with nothing on it but a phone and a folder. The woman behind it has silver hair in a low bun and does not stand. "You have walked up a flight of stairs into {tech_floor}, which is a licensed technical support service." She says it the way a clerk reads back an address. "I would like to know on whose authority."

choices.text: The authority of the people this floor called.
None yet. I came to ask you what this floor does.

soft_open.prompt: "It does what the sign says." She folds her hands on the folder. "Customers call us with a device problem. We walk them through it. We send an invoice. The invoices are on file, and the license is on the wall behind you." It is. It is real. That is the point of it.

choices.text: Then let's talk about the calls.

names_bea.prompt: "Miss Santiago is a probationary employee with a confidentiality agreement." No pause before the name, no pause after it. "Whatever she told you, she told you in breach of it, and I will be discussing that with her, not with you."

choices.text: Then let's discuss the calls instead.

deny_node.prompt: "Nobody on this floor dials out." She says it like a fact about the weather. "Customers call us. We have never made an outbound call in the history of this floor, and you will not find a phone bill that says otherwise." She has not looked at the folder once. She is not going to.
deny_node.claim: Rowena Ocampo, on the record: this floor makes no outbound calls; customers call in.
deny_node.evidence_hint: She has just told you the one thing this floor never does. One of the people this floor called has an account of being called back.

accepts_evidence.contradiction_note: Kevin Dizon dialed the number on a pop-up, was put on hold, and was called back nineteen minutes later by a technician using this floor's tool. A floor that never dials out dialed him.
accepts_evidence.response: She reads it. "A callback to a customer who requested support." She reads it again, and the second time is slower, and the folder is suddenly something she is looking at. "That is not an outbound call." It is.
"Miss Santiago." She says the name as if filing it. "Probationary. Confidentiality agreement." She does not read the rest, which means she already knows what is in it.
"Miss Lim applied and was not hired." She hands it back. "That is not a crime. That happens every week." It happened, that week, to an applicant who paid a fee to a floor that never called her back.
She reads it without expression. "A complaint. We receive them. They go to accounting." Accounting is, as far as anybody on either floor knows, at the head office on Terminal Road.

"A building pass." She holds it up to the light, once. "We issue them. It proves she works here, which I have never denied." A pass is a fact about a door, not about what happens on the other side of it.

choices.text: Every page of the script in that rack is initialed R.O.

caught_callback.prompt: For the first time she does not have the next sentence ready. "A callback," she says again, to the folder. "From your floor's support tool," you say, "to a man who called a number off a pop-up and wanted nothing but to close it." She closes the folder, which is the first thing she has done with it.

milestone.title: Account Broken: The Floor That Never Dials Out
milestone.detail: Rowena Ocampo's denial - customers call in, nobody dials out - did not survive a customer who was called back from her own floor's tool.

choices.text: Now the script. Every page is initialed R.O.

bea_node.prompt: "She told me about the recruitment folder by the door," you say. Rowena looks at the folder by the door, and does not look away from it fast enough. "Probationary employees see a great many things they do not understand." "She understood the two columns," you say. "Who paid the fee, and who got hired. They never share a name."

milestone.title: The Recruit Named The Folder
milestone.detail: Bea Santiago's statement put the recruitment folder in front of the director who keeps it - the fourth floor's hiring and its job-offer script are the same document.

choices.text: And every page of the script is initialed R.O.

pressed.prompt: "You have a complaint and a story. I have a business license." She turns the folder face down, which is not the same as putting it away. "Is there anything else?"

choices.text: There's the script in that rack with your initials on every page.

pressure_node.prompt: "Initials are not a confession. A script is not a crime. A callback is not an outbound call." She lists them without heat, like the terms of a lease. "You are describing a business that does what the sign says. What you want is for me to describe something else, and I am not going to."

choices.text: Then let's talk about what the removal fee removed.
Then I'll come back with a warrant.

tactic_quiz.setup: You put the script's last step beside a customer's receipt. The script: [i]STEP 6 - THE REMOVAL FEE.[/i] The receipt: [i]MALWARE REMOVAL - P2,400. Threats removed: 3.[/i]
tactic_quiz.question: What did the removal fee pay to remove?

milestone.title: Tactic Identified: The Fee For Nothing
milestone.detail: Recognized that the fee at the end of the script pays to fix the problem the start of the script invented - the receipt bills for a result that could not have happened.

options.text: Nothing. The threats were invented in step one so that step six could charge for them.
options.feedback: That is the whole floor in two steps. A web page cannot scan a machine, so the three threats never existed; the 'removal' removed them; the fee paid for the removal. Every number on that receipt is real except the one that matters. A fee to fix a problem you were told about by the person charging the fee is the tell, whatever the problem is called.

options.text: Three infected files, as the receipt says.
options.feedback: There were no files. The count came from a pop-up, and a pop-up cannot count anything on a machine it cannot see. The receipt repeats the made-up number with a price attached, which is what makes it look like a record.

options.text: The support tool the operator installed.
options.feedback: The tool stayed. It was the operation's way in, not the customer's problem; nobody charges a fee to leave their own software behind. What was billed was a result that could not have happened.

options.text: The operator's time on the call.
options.feedback: Real support bills time and says so on the invoice. This receipt bills for threats removed - a result, and one that could not have happened. That is the difference between a service and a script.

end_named.prompt: Rowena Ocampo looks at the two statements on her desk - a customer this floor called, and an applicant this floor sorted - and at the door, and at the phone, and does not pick up the phone. "The floors are leased," she says at last. "ClearLine's and mine. From the company that owns the tower on Terminal Road." She writes the name on the back of the folder in block capitals, the way she must have watched a thousand customers write down a session code, and turns it toward you. {company}. "I run a floor. I do not own the building. If you want the owner, that is where he is."

grants_evidence.label: The Name Above The Floors
grants_evidence.description: {company} - the company that owns the tower and the site on Terminal Road, and this building, whose upper floors it leases to {call_floor} and {tech_floor}. Named by the fourth floor's director. "I run a floor. I do not own the building."
grants_evidence.tactic: An operation is owned by whoever signs the leases, not by whoever reads the scripts - and the owner's name is the one thing no call ever mentions.

milestone.title: The Owner Named
milestone.detail: Rowena Ocampo, faced with a witness from each of her floor's two scams, put a name to the company that owns the building - the operation has an owner, and the owner is not on either floor.

end_denied.prompt: Rowena has denied everything, calmly, and one statement from one of her floor's two scams is not enough to make her do otherwise. The name on the tower down the road stays a name on a sign.

end_stonewalled.prompt: "Do that." She has the phone in her hand before you reach the stairs. By the time you are back on the street the fourth floor's lights are off, and a sign on the stairwell door says the floor is closed for maintenance. It will reopen when you have stopped looking.

milestone.title: The Fourth Floor Goes Dark
milestone.detail: Threatened with a warrant, the fourth floor's director closed the floor and made a call. An operation with a license and a landlord can wait out an investigator who has nothing but a threat.
